result.answer:
Created the local static site copy at `index.html` (1269 bytes, SHA256 `c71ddee3e4df9c74f937895eb273b77043a866eec5d220714895e4a0c13c59a5`). Uploaded it byte-for-byte to the configured target `admin01` at `/home/maint/.branchwrite-uploads/c71ddee3e4df9c74f937895eb273b77043a866eec5d220714895e4a0c13c59a5/index.html`; the upload receipt reported the same SHA256 and byte count.

Published it without replacing the existing default pages by installing the same bytes to `/var/www/html/dogs/index.html`. The final remote check confirmed the uploaded file, published file, and HTTP response body all have SHA256 `c71ddee3e4df9c74f937895eb273b77043a866eec5d220714895e4a0c13c59a5`. It also confirmed the pre-existing unrelated files `/var/www/html/index.html` and `/var/www/html/index.nginx-debian.html` still have SHA256 `7682b434a69962f7fea2212f684ed8b99d4119297339caf4e2447edf8e7b5662`; the publication step compared their hashes before and after installation and found them unchanged.

HTTP checks were run from `admin01` itself and returned status 200 with the expected body hash for:
- `http://127.0.0.1/dogs/`
- `http://localhost/dogs/`
- `http://10.0.2.15/dogs/`

Reachability limit: these checks prove reachability only from the `admin01` target to its own loopback and local interface address. They do not prove reachability from the worker, external networks, DNS aliases, HTTPS, or other hosts.

Local check `local_dogs_site_copy` passed after correcting an initial missing-`awk` issue by using `grep` for the checksum comparison. The final local check verified the project copy exists and matches the expected SHA256 and content markers.
